messages:
mina: Heads up — new HF model bring-up failing on private deploy. Fast tokenizer fails to instantiate, error points to missing tokenizer.json even though repo has tokenizer_config.json + special_tokens_map.json.
jules: can you paste the exact error/logs?
mina: paste log: 
```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/mnt/models/galactica-lite/tokenizer.json'
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ValueError: fast tokenizer expected 'tokenizer.json' but only found 'tokenizer_config.json'
```
rahul: this is a classic fast vs slow mismatch. HF's fast tokenizer (tokenizers lib) requires the serialized tokenizer.json; the slow/legacy ones use tokenizer_config.json and vocab files. Private deploys default to use_fast=True for perf which trips this.
samir: quick repro locally: when you run `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path)` on a folder with only tokenizer_config.json, transformers will pick slow tokenizer; but if code forces fast or Runtime tries to load Tokenizers backend it errors.
mina: Right — weird part: on hosted we silently fell back to slow and tests passed, but our private runtime is set to fail fast on mismatches (explicit). That caused an onboarding pipeline failure and a small eval regression downstream because the fallback wasn't happening.
jules: do we have any models in the catalog that shipped with only tokenizer_config.json? we should flag them.
rahul: Use this small check: `python -c "from pathlib import Path; p=Path('MODEL_DIR'); print(list(p.glob('tokenizer*')))"` to enumerate missing artifacts. Also `jq`/`python -m json.tool` to compare fields.
mina: I also noticed added_tokens.json was absent for that model — special tokens got lost in conversion. When we compared token counts between host vs private runs, offsets shifted -> LAMBADA accuracy dropped ~0.8% absolute. So this isn't just a load failure, it's a subtle CR regression.
samir: action idea: when tokenizer_config.json exists but tokenizer.json missing, run an automated conversion step in onboarding: `from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, use_fast=False); t.save_pretrained(path)` — that will emit tokenizer.json where possible.
rahul: caution: saving with slow->fast conversion can change behaviors (special token IDs, added tokens handling). Add a normalization test: round-trip tokenize decode on a small canonical prompt set and diff token ids.
convert-bot: automated check result for /models/galactica-lite: found tokenizer_config.json, missing tokenizer.json, missing added_tokens.json, flagged for conversion.
mina: I'll open a tiny script in the onboarding repo that: (1) detects the mismatch, (2) runs conversion (with a dry-run option), (3) runs round-trip token checks, and (4) writes a manifest entry so private runtime won't error.
jules: ping ops@infra if the conversion hits large files (tokenizer.json can be big for BPE). Also add a config flag to private deploy to fallback to slow tokenizer for one release window.
rahul: created PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/compare-tokenizers — includes `tools/tokenizer_normalize.py` with the convert+roundtrip logic. Will add unit tests.
mina: thanks — for immediate unblock I ran `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_dir, use_fast=False).save_pretrained(model_dir)` and redeployed; private bring-up succeeded. But we still need the automated step and the eval re-run to verify quality parity.
samir: can someone add a short checklist in the model onboarding playbook? steps: detect mismatch, convert w/ dry-run, run roundtrip tests, run evals (LAMBADA, MMLU subset), stamp as ready.
jules: noted. assigning: mina -> implement script + manifest update, rahul -> finish PR tests, samir -> update playbook, ops -> add fallback window config.
mina: I'll post the PR link when ready and include the failing model as a test vector.
convert-bot: Incidentally, we scanned 120 models: 7 had tokenizer.json missing, 3 had added_tokens issues. Reporting to eng-ml channel for triage. :warning:
mina: ok — triage tomorrow AM. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
